# `shell/gpu-ui/GPUWindowCapture.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/shell/gpu-ui/GPUWindowCapture.js`

GPUWindowCapture.js — live per-window content via the Element Capture API. Chrome 132+ lets us restrict a getDisplayMedia track to a single DOM element (RestrictionTarget + track.restrictTo), yielding a live MediaStream of just that element's rendered subtree (no occlusion / "hall of mirrors"). We take ONE getDisplayMedia('this tab') stream, clone its track per window, restrict each clone to that app's panel element, and feed a hidden <video>. The GPU compositor then copyExternalImageToTexture()s each video frame into the window's content-atlas region every frame → fully live GPU windows. Requirements (per spec) on each captured element: it must form a stacking context (isolation:isolate) and be flattened (transform-style:flat) with an opaque background. Desktop applies these before attaching. Gracefully unsupported on non-Chromium / older builds (supported=false) so callers fall back to extension snapshot, then native chrome.

### `class GPUWindowCapture`

Chrome 132+ lets us restrict a getDisplayMedia track to a single DOM element (RestrictionTarget + track.restrictTo), yielding a live MediaStream of just that element's rendered subtree (no occlusion / "hall of mirrors"). ## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
